page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Printed page number at the top left. Running head centred at the top. Catchword at the bottom right. Red stains in the left margin are not printed and are left out.

main_text.l: nulla possit assignari causa, nec sane alia fit, fatean-
tur quod verum est, partes alias in misto fuisse, qua-
rum segregatione reliquæ siccæ apparuerint, qua-
rum ficcitas cum humidis confusa non patebat: ut
si liquorem quo pannus aut aliquid aliud madeat,
elicias, pannus ficcus erit qui prius madidus, par-
tium scilicet humidarum segregatione.
Id ipsum possemus ostendere in refrigeratione,
quæ fit plerumque partium calidarum separatione.
Idcirco Aristoteles in problematis quærens, cur
aqua calida citius ad radios Solis refrigeretur, quam
in loco frigido posita, rationem assignat, quod ca-
lor vehementior evincat infirmiorem, hoc experiun-
tur, qui sudantes accedunt ad ignem, ut sudare desi-
nant, & qui manum adustam igni admovent, quo ci-
tius curentur. Id ipsum feliciter experti sunt mili-
tes illi quos refert Ambrosius Pareus, qui à pulvere
tormentario accenso ambusti; quod medicorum
manus nil prodesset, desperatione vicli[?] ad flumen
se præcipites daturi cum currerent, ab anu quadam
obvia cæparum admotarum beneficio, miraculosè sa-
nati sunt.
Vnde & Ferneliusait, cæpas ambusta per miracu-
lum sanare, quas tamen valde calidas esse gustus do-
cet. Hoc facit & Sambuci cortex, vel ejus succus qui
licet calidus, & siccus ordine secundo, his aliisque
inflammationibus mirificè confert, quas & calx ipsa
ex melle admota sedat; ut, cujus aqua licet admodum
calida, veluti id genus alia permulta, ambusta sanat;
Quæ quidem, ut Fernelius de cæpis, miracula sunt,
sed iis, qui actionum naturalium vera ignorant prin-
cipia. Quorum omnium facilis esset ratio, si scirent
partes calidas per adustionem solutas, apertionem
pororum quo liberius exeant, requirere, qua caloris
externi beneficio, impetrata erumpant partem affli-
ctam infestare definentes?
Verùm

page.notes: Red marks on the left margin and elsewhere are stains, not printed text, and are not transcribed. "vicli[?]" is uncertain: the printed word may be "victi". "Ferneliusait" is kept as printed, probably for "Fernelius ait". The catchword "Verùm" is given in the bottom margin and also appears as the closing word line in main_text, which may be a duplicate; the text ends with "definentes?".
